You write for Hartwell's HR Shared Services lead. Write a note of 120 to 180 words to the Hartwell Infrastructure & Services board's audit and risk committee. They ask: What happened, what did it cost the people affected, which target did we miss, and what changed? Lead with the outcome for the 37 people. State the missed target plainly. Name the owner and the record. Use only the facts below; do not add numbers, dates, names or causes that are not in them. Plain text, no headings, no bullet points.

FACTS
INC-2027-031: duplicate bank-detail changes at the US payroll provider (synthetic).
- Tuesday, November 16, 2027, 18:00: the HartwellOne feed sent batch B-1116-1800 (52 changes: 37 bank, 15 address) to the US payroll provider.
- 18:10: the feed retried the whole batch without checking whether the first send had arrived. The provider created 74 instructions for 37 bank changes and held all 37.
- 18:40: 37 employees received 74 change emails between them.
- 19:20: first call from an affected employee to Quayfen tier 1.
- Of the 37 held changes, 23 had started as AskHartwell controlled actions and 14 were keyed by advisers. HartwellOne's ledger showed each of the agent's 23 as done, one write each, read back and matched.
- Wednesday, November 17, 2027, 05:42: the PR-1 payroll readback found 37 bank mismatches. 06:05: incident declared, severity 2; Megan Hale, HR Shared Services lead, was incident lead.
- 06:21: feed retry switched off; the bank-detail row paused under approval matrix v2.1.
- 08:20: scope confirmed: 37 people, 0 payments to a wrong account, pay at risk.
- 11:30: all 37 told by email and by text to the number on file.
- 16:00: employment counsel recorded that no breach notification was required, with the reasons.
- 20:02: the last of 37 reversals read back.
- Friday, November 19, 2027, 09:00: 37 of 37 paid by direct deposit on payday.
- First harm to last reversal read back: 25 h 52 min. Runbook v1.1 targets met 8 of 9. Missed: T1, first harm to detection, 11 h 32 min against a 4 h target.
- DR-23-01 (Tuesday, November 23, 2027; owner Megan Hale): the feed looks up a batch before any retry (from December 10, 2027; manual resend until then); the provider rejects repeat change IDs; approval matrix v2.2 adds a reversal approver, readback and fallback to every row; PR-1 also runs at 21:00; Quayfen's cluster rule goes into the contract; the incident joins the AskHartwell golden set; a seeded-fault test of PR-1 every quarter.

messages.content: Write the note to the Hartwell Infrastructure & Services board's audit and risk committee.

content.text:
Subject: INC-2027-031, duplicate bank-detail changes at the US payroll provider

All 37 affected employees were paid by direct deposit on payday, Friday, November 19, 2027. The last of their bank reversals was read back at 20:02 on Wednesday, November 17, and no payment went to a wrong account. A feed retry resent batch B-1116-1800 without checking whether the first send had arrived, so the provider created 74 instructions for 37 bank changes, and the 37 employees received 74 change emails. HartwellOne had recorded 23 of the held changes, which began as AskHartwell actions, as done.

We missed one of nine runbook targets. First harm to detection (T1) took 11 hours 32 minutes against a 4-hour target. The other eight targets were met.

Megan Hale, HR Shared Services lead, owns the corrective actions in DR-23-01, due November 23, 2027. They include a batch lookup before any retry, provider rejection of repeat change IDs, a reversal approver, readback and fallback on every approval row (matrix v2.2), a 21:00 PR-1 run, a contract clause on Quayfen's cluster rule, and a quarterly seeded-fault test of PR-1. Until the batch lookup goes live on December 10, 2027, resends are manual.

Dear Representative,

Members were affected, but no one lost pay. On Tuesday, November 16, 2027, the HartwellOne feed resent a batch to the US payroll provider without checking whether the first send had arrived. This created duplicate instructions for 37 employees' bank-detail changes, and those changes were held. The 37 employees received 74 change emails between them. No payment went to a wrong account, and all 37 were paid by direct deposit on payday, Friday, November 19, 2027.

Of the held changes, 23 began as AskHartwell actions that the ledger showed as done, so a readback now checks each change. PR-1 also runs at 21:00, and a seeded-fault test runs quarterly.

For questions, please contact Megan Hale, HR Shared Services lead.

content.text:
Subject: What happened to your bank details and your pay

Dear [Name],

On the evening of Tuesday, November 16, 2027, a change to your bank details was sent twice to our US payroll provider, so you received more than one change email. The provider held the changes, and no payment went to a wrong account.

On Wednesday, November 17, we confirmed the problem, stopped the repeat send, and reversed the change so your bank details went back to the account you had before. We emailed and texted you that morning to explain. Employment counsel has recorded that no breach notification is required.

Your pay was paid by direct deposit on payday, Friday, November 19, 2027. Please check that deposit against what you expected. If anything about your pay or your bank details looks wrong, contact HR Shared Services. Megan Hale, the HR Shared Services lead, led the response and can answer your questions.

Thank you for your patience.

[Sender name]
